paginas.es: En Puerto Suma, las noticias viajaban a dos velocidades: la del periódico, que salía los domingos, y la de Nora Vidal, que salía cada vez que abría la boca. La llamaban Radio Nora, y a ella le encantaba. ¿Sabes lo que hace una radio, sumanauta, cuando oye solo media frase? Se inventa la otra media. Y eso pasó un martes, en la panadería.
paginas.en: In Puerto Suma, news travelled at two speeds: the speed of the newspaper, which came out on Sundays, and the speed of Nora Vidal, which came out every time she opened her mouth. They called her Radio Nora, and she loved it. Do you know what a radio does, Sumanaut, when it picks up only half a sentence? It makes up the other half. And that's what happened one Tuesday, at the bakery.

paginas.es: Nora esperaba su barra mientras, detrás de la cortina del obrador, el panadero Remigio cuchicheaba con su hija Candela. —A la alcaldesa le ha llegado la hora de irse —decía él—. El sábado la sacamos delante de todo el pueblo, en la plaza. Y el faro lo partimos allí mismo. —Pero que no se nos derrita —dijo Candela. —Chist. Ni una palabra. Ella no sabe que lo sabemos.
paginas.en: Nora was waiting for her loaf while, behind the curtain to the back room, Remigio the baker was whispering with his daughter Candela. "The mayor's time to go has come," he was saying. "On Saturday we bring her out in front of the whole town, in the square. And we split the lighthouse right there." "As long as it doesn't melt on us," said Candela. "Shh. Not a word. She doesn't know we know."

paginas.es: Nora salió con la barra bajo el brazo y el corazón a mil. ¡Un complot! ¡Contra doña Eulalia, la alcaldesa de toda la vida, que no había dicho nada de irse! ¿Y partir el faro? Se lo contó a Óscar, su mejor amigo, que estaba en el muelle comiendo pipas. —Solo a ti, ¿eh? Óscar escupió una cáscara al agua. —¿Y tú cómo sabes que significa lo que crees?
paginas.en: Nora left with the loaf under her arm and her heart racing. A plot! Against Doña Eulalia, the mayor they'd had forever, who had never said a word about leaving! And splitting the lighthouse? She told Óscar, her best friend, who was on the pier eating sunflower seeds. "Just you, okay?" Óscar spat a shell into the water. "And how do you know it means what you think?"
